author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Catholic Medical Center has awarded Granite United Way a $25,000 grant aimed at supporting Manchester children, new mothers and first responders through several community programs.

The hospital said the funding will help provide back-to-school resources and supplies, infant-safety education and kits for new mothers and babies. It also will support mental-health training designed for emergency personnel who routinely encounter traumatic events.

According to the hospital, the grant will fund multiple day-long training sessions for nearly 100 first responders and expand outreach intended to reach more than 100 families. The award is part of a broader $2 million community commitment by CMC parent HCA Healthcare.

The projects address different needs but share an early-intervention focus: giving families practical supplies at vulnerable moments and helping responders recognize and manage the strain of emergency work. Because the announcement describes planned services, the next useful measures will be participation, delivery of the promised resources and whether the programs continue after this grant period.
dek: A $25,000 grant to Granite United Way will fund school resources, infant-safety supplies and mental-health training for first responders.
headline: Catholic Medical Center grant expands Manchester family and first-responder support
